u7-l1.0.note.en: Idem na prednášku. = I'm going to a lecture. At a lecture: **na prednáške**.
u7-l1.0.note.t: Idem na prednášku. = Maʼruzaga ketyapman. Maʼruzada: **na prednáške**.

u7-l1.1.note.en: A class where students discuss and present. At a seminar: **na seminári**.
u7-l1.1.note.t: Talabalar mavzuni muhokama qiladigan va chiqish qiladigan dars. Seminarda: **na seminári**.

u7-l1.3.note.en: In the library: **v knižnici**. **čítať** = to read (čítam, čítaš, číta…), **kniha** = book: čítam knihu.
u7-l1.3.note.t: Kutubxonada: **v knižnici**. **čítať** = oʻqimoq (čítam, čítaš, číta…), **kniha** = kitob: čítam knihu = kitob oʻqiyapman.

u7-l1.4.en.en: Emma is in the library, reading a book.

u7-l1.4.why.en: For being in a place, the word changes after v or na: in the library is **v knižnici**, like na prednáške. Knižnica is the plain form.
u7-l1.4.why.t: Biror joyda ekanini aytganda soʻz v yoki na soʻzidan keyin oʻzgaradi, oʻzbekchadagi -da kabi: kutubxonada — **v knižnici**, xuddi na prednáške kabi. Knižnica — oddiy shakl.

u7-l1.5.note.en: **hodina** is an hour, and also one class period.

u7-l1.7.note.en: Mám skúšku. = I have an exam. **zajtra** = tomorrow.

u7-l1.8.note.en: A short talk or paper for a seminar. **písať** = to write (píšem, píšeš, píše…): Píšem referát. = I'm writing a paper.
u7-l1.8.note.t: Seminar uchun qisqa chiqish yoki yozma ish. **písať** = yozmoq (píšem, píšeš, píše…): Píšem referát. = Referat yozyapman.

u7-l1.9.why.en: The exam is what you have, the object, so skúška changes -a to **-u**: mám **skúšku**.
u7-l1.9.why.t: Imtihon — sizda bor narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun skúška soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: mám **skúšku**.

en: Lucia is ona, and with on or ona the verb has no ending: **píše**. Píšem is the ja form.
Lucia writes one paper, so it's **referát**: as the object, a masculine thing stays the same. Referáty is the plural, papers.
t: Lusiya haqida «u» — ona, on yoki ona bilan esa feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: **píše**. Píšem — ja shakli.
Lusiya bitta referat yozyapti, shuning uchun **referát**: erkak jinsidagi narsa toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi. Referáty — koʻplik, «referatlar».

u7-l1.11.en.en: Today I have a lecture and a seminar.

u7-l1.12.note.en: **meškať** = to be late. A kind reply: **To sa stáva.** (It happens.)
u7-l1.12.note.t: **meškať** = kechikmoq. Muloyim javob: **To sa stáva.** (Boʻlib turadi.)

u7-l1.13.question.en: Emma comes in late. What does pani Horváthová say?
u7-l1.13.question.t: Emma kechikib keldi. Horvatova xonim nima deydi?

u7-l1.14.why.en: Prepáčte is formal vy, to the teacher, but the one who's late is ja (I), so the verb ends in **-m**: mešk**ám**.
u7-l1.14.why.t: Prepáčte — oʻqituvchiga hurmatli vy, lekin kechikayotgan — ja (men), shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi: mešk**ám**.

en: Prepáčte is formal vy, but the one who's late is ja (I), so the verb ends in **-m**: mešk**ám**. Meškáš is the ty form.
Sorry is **Prepáčte**, the vy form of prepáč, for a teacher or a stranger. Prosím means please.
t: Prepáčte — hurmatli vy, lekin kechikkan — ja (men), shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi: mešk**ám**. Meškáš — ty shakli.
«Kechirasiz» — **Prepáčte**, prepáč soʻzining vy shakli, oʻqituvchi yoki notanish odam uchun. Prosím esa «iltimos» degani.

en: The word **hodina** (hour) changes its ending with the number.
t: 1: **je … hodina**. 2–4: **sú … hodiny**. 5 va undan koʻp: **je … hodín**. Feʼl ham oʻzgaradi: je yoki sú.

u7-l2.2.why.en: With 2, 3 and 4 it's **sú** and hodin**y**. Je jedna hodina is 1:00, and je päť hodín is 5:00.
u7-l2.2.why.t: 2, 3 va 4 bilan **sú** va hodin**y** keladi. Je jedna hodina — 1:00, je päť hodín esa 5:00.

u7-l2.3.why.en: From 5 up, hodina becomes **hodín**, with je. Hodiny goes with 2–4, hodina with 1.
u7-l2.3.why.t: 5 dan boshlab hodina **hodín** boʻladi, je bilan. Hodiny 2–4 bilan, hodina esa 1 bilan keladi.

u7-l2.4.note.en: The answer uses **o** and a special form of the number: o jednej, o druhej…
u7-l2.4.note.t: Javobda **o** va sonning maxsus shakli ishlatiladi: o jednej (soat birda), o druhej (soat ikkida)…

en: To say at what time, use **o** and a form ending in **-ej**. Most of them come from “second, third…”, so they don't look exactly like the numbers.
Also: o štvrtej (4), o šiestej (6), o jedenástej (11), o dvanástej (12).
t: Soat nechada ekanini aytish uchun **o** va **-ej** bilan tugaydigan shaklni ishlating (oʻzbekchadagi «soat beshda» kabi). Ularning koʻpi tartib sonlardan («ikkinchi, uchinchi…») yasalgan, shuning uchun oddiy sonlarga unchalik oʻxshamaydi.
Yana: o štvrtej (4), o šiestej (6), o jedenástej (11), o dvanástej (12).

en: At a time is **o** + the **-ej** form: o deviat**ej**. Deväť is the plain number, for counting.
Hodín is for telling the time: je deväť hodín, it's nine o'clock. To say when something is, use o + the **-ej** form: o deviat**ej**.
t: Soat nechada ekanini aytish uchun **o** + **-ej** shakli keladi: o deviat**ej** (soat toʻqqizda). Deväť — oddiy son, sanash uchun.
Hodín soat necha ekanini aytganda ishlatiladi: je deväť hodín — soat toʻqqiz. Biror narsa qachon boʻlishini aytish uchun esa o + **-ej** shakli keladi: o deviat**ej**.

u7-l2.8.note.en: Slovak looks ahead: **pol ôsmej** is “half of the eighth hour”. At 7:30 = **o pol ôsmej**.
u7-l2.8.note.t: Slovak tili oldinga qaraydi: **pol ôsmej** — «sakkizinchi soatning yarmi». Oʻzbekchada esa «yetti yarim» deymiz. Soat yetti yarimda = **o pol ôsmej**.

u7-l2.9.why.en: Slovak looks ahead: **pol desiatej** is half of the tenth hour, so 9:30. 10:30 would be pol jedenástej.
u7-l2.9.why.t: Slovaklar oldinga qarab hisoblaydi: **pol desiatej** — «oʻninchi soatning yarmi», yaʼni 9:30. 10:30 esa pol jedenástej boʻlardi.

u7-l2.10.note.en: Literally “a quarter towards nine”. 8:45 is **trištvrte na deväť**.
u7-l2.10.note.t: Soʻzma-soʻz: «toʻqqiz tomon chorak», yaʼni toʻqqizinchi soatning birinchi choragi. Diqqat: bu 8:15, oʻzbekchadagi «toʻqqizga chorak qoldi» (8:45) emas! 8:45 esa **trištvrte na deväť** («toʻqqiz tomon uch chorak»).

u7-l2.11.why.en: **Štvrť** na deväť is a quarter of the way towards nine, so 8:15. Trištvrte (three quarters) na deväť is 8:45.
u7-l2.11.why.t: Slovaklar keyingi soatga qarab hisoblaydi: **štvrť** na deväť — toʻqqizinchi soatning choragi oʻtdi, yaʼni 8:15. Trištvrte (uch chorak) na deväť esa 8:45.

u7-l2.12.why.en: Three quarters of the way to nine is **trištvrte** na deväť. Štvrť na deväť is 8:15, and pol deviatej is 8:30.
u7-l2.12.why.t: Toʻqqizinchi soatning uch choragi oʻtdi — **trištvrte** na deväť, yaʼni 8:45. Štvrť na deväť — 8:15, pol deviatej esa 8:30.

u7-l2.13.en.en: The lecture is at half past eight.

en: **Koľko je hodín?** is a set question, literally “how many hours is it?”, with the form used from 5 up. Hodiny goes with 2–4.
Asking the time is **Koľko** je hodín?, literally “how many hours?”. Kedy means when: Kedy je seminár?
t: **Koľko je hodín?** — tayyor savol, soʻzma-soʻz «necha soat bor?», 5 dan boshlab ishlatiladigan shakl bilan. Hodiny 2–4 bilan keladi.
Vaqtni soʻrash — **Koľko** je hodín?, soʻzma-soʻz «necha soat?». Kedy esa «qachon»: Kedy je seminár?

u7-l2.15.why.en: At a time is **o** + the **-ej** form: o siedm**ej**. Sedem is the plain number, for counting.
u7-l2.15.why.t: Soat nechada ekanini aytish uchun **o** + **-ej** shakli keladi: o siedm**ej** (soat yettida). Sedem — oddiy son, sanash uchun.

u7-l3.0.en.en: In the morning I get up at seven.

u7-l3.0.note.en: **vstávať** = to get up: vstávam, vstávaš, vstáva…

u7-l3.1.note.en: And then: **obliekam sa** = I get dressed. Both use **sa**.
u7-l3.1.note.t: Keyin: **obliekam sa** = kiyinaman. Ikkalasida ham **sa** bor: harakat oʻzingizga qaratilgan, oʻzbekchadagi yuvinmoq, kiyinmoq soʻzlaridagi -in kabi.

u7-l3.2.question.en: Emma says this. What is she doing?
u7-l3.2.question.t: Emma shunday deydi. U nima qilyapti?

u7-l3.5.en.en: First I shower, then I have breakfast.
u7-l3.5.en.t: Avval dush qabul qilaman, keyin nonushta qilaman.

u7-l3.6.en.en: First I get dressed, then I have breakfast.

u7-l3.6.why.en: **Najprv** is first and **potom** is then. Najprv is already used for getting dressed, so breakfast comes **potom**.
u7-l3.6.why.t: **Najprv** — «avval», **potom** — «keyin». Najprv kiyinish uchun ishlatilgan, shuning uchun nonushta **potom** keladi.

en: At a time is **o** + the **-ej** form: o siedm**ej**. Sedem is the plain number, for counting.
“I” is ja, so the verb ends in **-m**: vstáva**m**. Vstávaš, with -š, is the ty form (you).
t: Soat nechada ekanini aytish uchun **o** + **-ej** shakli keladi: o siedm**ej** (soat yettida). Sedem — oddiy son, sanash uchun.
«Men» — ja, shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi: vstáva**m** (turaman). -š bilan vstávaš — ty (sen) shakli.

u7-l3.8.en.en: In the morning I have lectures.

u7-l3.8.note.en: **doobeda** = before noon, **naobed** = at lunchtime, **poobede** = in the afternoon, **v noci** = at night.
u7-l3.8.note.t: **doobeda** = tushgacha, **naobed** = tushlik paytida, **poobede** = tushdan keyin, **v noci** = kechasi.

u7-l3.10.note.en: **učiť sa** = to study, to learn: učím sa, učíš sa, učí sa… Don't drop the **sa**: učiť alone means to teach (like učiteľ, teacher).
u7-l3.10.note.t: **učiť sa** = oʻqimoq, oʻrganmoq, dars qilmoq: učím sa, učíš sa, učí sa… **sa** soʻzini tushirib qoldirmang: učiť yolgʻiz oʻzi «oʻrgatmoq» degani (učiteľ — oʻqituvchi soʻzi ham shundan). Xuddi oʻrganmoq va oʻrgatmoq kabi.

u7-l3.11.en.en: In the afternoon I study in the library.

u7-l3.12.en.en: Emma has breakfast at half past seven.
u7-l3.12.en.t: Emma soat yetti yarimda nonushta qiladi.

u7-l3.12.why.en: With **on** or **ona**, the verb has no ending: Emma **raňajkuje**. Raňajkujem goes with ja, raňajkujú with oni.
u7-l3.12.why.t: **on** yoki **ona** bilan feʼl qoʻshimchasiz keladi: Emma **raňajkuje**. Raňajkujem ja bilan, raňajkujú esa oni bilan keladi.

u7-l3.13.en.en: In the evening I'm tired. (woman speaking)

u7-l3.13.note.en: A man says: Večer som **unavený**. Then it's time for **idem spať** = I'm going to bed.
u7-l3.13.note.t: Sifat gapiruvchining jinsiga qarab oʻzgaradi. Erkak kishi: Večer som **unavený**. Keyin esa **idem spať** = uxlagani yotaman.

u7-l3.14.en.en: Tomáš is tired in the evening.

u7-l3.14.why.en: Adjectives agree with the person: Tomáš is a man, so **unavený**. Unavená is for a woman: Večer som unavená, says Emma.
u7-l3.14.why.t: Sifat odamga moslashadi: Tomash — erkak, shuning uchun **unavený**. Unavená — ayol uchun: Emma «Večer som unavená» deydi.

u7-l3.15.prompt.en: First I study, then I go to bed.
u7-l3.15.prompt.t: Avval dars qilaman, keyin uxlagani yotaman.

en: It's ja (I) who studies, so the verb ends in **-m**: najprv sa uč**ím**. Učíš is the ty form (you).
It's ja (I) going to bed, so ísť is **idem**: idem spať. Ideme is the my form (we).
t: Dars qiladigan — ja (men), shuning uchun feʼl **-m** bilan tugaydi: najprv sa uč**ím**. Učíš — ty (sen) shakli.
Uxlagani yotadigan — ja (men), shuning uchun ísť **idem** boʻladi: idem spať. Ideme — my (biz) shakli.

en: In the evening Lucia reads a book.
Lucia reads a book in the evening.
In the evening Lucia is reading a book.
Lucia is reading a book in the evening.

u7-l3.17.en.en: I get up at seven in the morning.

en: Three more present-tense patterns. **spať** (to sleep) and **vidieť** (to see) take **-ím**; **stretnúť** (to meet) takes **-em**.
**stretnúť** is one complete action, so its present form talks about the future: **stretnem** = I'll meet. With **sa** it means to meet up: Kde sa stretneme?
t: Hozirgi zamonda tuslanishning yana uchta namunasi. **spať** (uxlamoq) va **vidieť** (koʻrmoq) **-ím** oladi; **stretnúť** (uchratmoq) esa **-em** oladi.

**stretnúť** — tugallangan tur: bir martalik, oxiriga yetadigan harakat. Shuning uchun uning hozirgi zamon shakli kelasi zamonni bildiradi: **stretnem** = uchrataman (keyinroq). **sa** bilan «uchrashmoq» degani: Kde sa stretneme? = Qayerda uchrashamiz?

u7-l4.1.en.en: It's morning and Lucia is asleep.

u7-l4.1.why.en: Lucia is ona, and the ona form of spať is **spí**. Spia goes with oni, spím with ja.
u7-l4.1.why.t: Lusiya — ona, spať feʼlining ona shakli esa **spí**. Spia oni bilan, spím esa ja bilan keladi.

u7-l4.2.why.en: With **my** (we) the verb ends in **-me**: sp**íme**. Spia goes with oni, spí with on or ona.
u7-l4.2.why.t: **my** (biz) bilan feʼl **-me** bilan tugaydi: sp**íme** (uxlaymiz). Spia oni bilan, spí esa on yoki ona bilan keladi.

u7-l4.4.why.en: With **ja**, stretnúť ends in **-em**, and as one complete action it talks about the future: stretn**em** = I'll meet. Stretne is on or ona, stretnú oni.
u7-l4.4.why.t: **ja** bilan stretnúť **-em** bilan tugaydi va bir martalik, tugallangan harakat sifatida kelasi zamonni bildiradi: stretn**em** = uchrataman. Stretne — on yoki ona, stretnú — oni.

en: “We” is my, so stretnúť ends in **-eme**: stretn**eme**. Stretnem is the ja form: I'll meet.
Where? is **Kde**. Kedy means when: Kedy sa stretneme? = When shall we meet?
t: «Biz» — my, shuning uchun stretnúť **-eme** bilan tugaydi: stretn**eme** (uchrashamiz). Stretnem — ja shakli: «uchrataman».
«Qayerda?» — **Kde**. Kedy esa «qachon»: Kedy sa stretneme? = Qachon uchrashamiz?

en: These verbs follow the same three patterns. Learn each one with its ja form.
Like stretnúť, **zaspať, stihnúť** and **zabudnúť** are one complete action, so their present forms talk about the future: zabudnem = I'll forget.
t: Bu feʼllar oʻsha uch namuna boʻyicha tuslanadi. Har birini ja shakli bilan birga yodlang.

stretnúť kabi, **zaspať, stihnúť** va **zabudnúť** ham bir martalik, tugallangan harakatni bildiradi, shuning uchun ularning hozirgi zamon shakli kelasi zamon maʼnosida keladi: zabudnem = unutib qoʻyaman.

u7-l4.7.en.en: It's half past seven. Will we make the bus?

u7-l4.7.why.en: With **my** (we), stihnúť ends in **-eme**: stihn**eme**. Stihnem goes with ja, stihnú with oni.
u7-l4.7.why.t: **my** (biz) bilan stihnúť **-eme** bilan tugaydi: stihn**eme** (ulguramiz). Stihnem ja bilan, stihnú esa oni bilan keladi.

u7-l4.8.en.en: Emma is sitting in the library.

en: With ja (I), sedieť ends in **-ím**: sed**ím**. Sedí is the on or ona form.
In the library is **v knižnici**: after v, for being in a place, the word changes its ending. Knižnica is the plain form.
t: «Men» — ja, ja bilan esa sedieť **-ím** bilan tugaydi: sed**ím** (oʻtiribman). Sedí — on yoki ona shakli.
«Kutubxonada» — **v knižnici**: biror joyda ekanini aytganda v soʻzidan keyin soʻzning oxiri oʻzgaradi, oʻzbekchadagi -da kabi. Knižnica — oddiy shakl.

u7-l4.10.en.en: What are you thinking about, Lucia?

u7-l4.10.why.en: The question is to Lucia, so it's **ty**, and the verb ends in **-š**: mysl**íš**. Myslí would be talking about her (ona).
u7-l4.10.why.t: Savol Lusiyaga berilyapti, demak **ty**, feʼl esa **-š** bilan tugaydi: mysl**íš**. Myslí u haqida (ona) gapirganda ishlatiladi.

en: To talk about the past, take the infinitive, drop **-ť** and add **-l** (he), **-la** (she), **-lo** (it) or **-li** (they, any gender).
So the past form shows who did it: Tomáš robi**l**, Lucia robi**la**. **včera** = yesterday.
t: Oʻtgan zamon haqida gapirish uchun feʼlning lugʻatdagi shaklini (infinitívni) oling va oxiridagi **-ť** oʻrniga **-l** (u, erkak), **-la** (u, ayol), **-lo** (u, oʻrta jins) yoki **-li** (ular, har qanday jins) qoʻying.
Shunday qilib, oʻtgan zamon shakli ishni kim qilganini — erkakmi yoki ayolmi — koʻrsatadi: Tomáš robi**l** (Tomash qildi), Lucia robi**la** (Lusiya qildi). **včera** = kecha.

u7-l5.1.title.en: I and you: add som, si, sme, ste
u7-l5.1.title.t: Men, sen, biz, siz: som, si, sme, ste

en: With **ja, ty, my, vy**, add the short form of **byť**: som, si, sme, ste. With **on, ona, oni**, add nothing.
This little word goes second in the sentence: Včera **som** pracovala. Pracovala **som** doma.
Formal **vy** always takes **-li**, even for one person: Čo **ste** robili, pani Horváthová?
t: **ja, ty, my, vy** bilan **byť** (boʻlmoq) feʼlining qisqa shaklini qoʻshing: som, si, sme, ste. Ular oʻzbekchadagi -m, -ng, -k, -ngiz (ishladim, ishlading, ishladik, ishladingiz) kabi shaxsni bildiradi. **on, ona, oni** bilan hech narsa qoʻshilmaydi.
Bu kichik soʻz gapda ikkinchi oʻrinda turadi: Včera **som** pracovala. Pracovala **som** doma.
Hurmat shakli **vy** (siz) bitta odamga ham doim **-li** bilan keladi: Čo **ste** robili, pani Horváthová? = Nima qildingiz, Horvatova xonim?

en: What did you do? (to a man)

u7-l5.2.why.en: Lucia is a woman, so the past tense ends in **-la**: písal**a**. Písal is for a man, písali for more people.
u7-l5.2.why.t: Lusiya — ayol, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi: písal**a**. Písal erkak, písali esa bir necha kishi uchun. Oʻzbekchada «yozdi» hammaga bir xil.

u7-l5.3.question.en: Emma wants to say “I studied yesterday.” Which is right?
u7-l5.3.question.t: Emma «Kecha dars qildim» demoqchi. Qaysi biri toʻgʻri?

u7-l5.3.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the past tense ends in **-la**: učil**a**. And ja needs **som**: without it, učila is about someone else (ona).
u7-l5.3.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi: učil**a**. ja uchun esa **som** kerak (oʻzbekchadagi -m kabi): usiz učila boshqa ayol (ona) haqida boʻladi.

en: A woman is speaking, so the past tense ends in **-la**: pracoval**a**. Pracoval is for a man.
With ja (I), the past tense adds **som**, in second place: včera **som** pracovala. Si goes with ty (you).
t: Ayol gapiryapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi: pracoval**a**. Pracoval — erkak uchun; oʻzbekchada «ishladim» ikkalasiga bir xil.
«Men» uchun oʻtgan zamonga **som** qoʻshiladi, gapda ikkinchi oʻrinda: včera **som** pracovala. U «ishladim»dagi -m vazifasini bajaradi; si esa ty (sen) uchun.

u7-l5.5.en.en: Emma, what did you do yesterday?

u7-l5.5.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the past tense ends in **-la**: robil**a**. Robil is for a man, robili for more people or formal vy.
u7-l5.5.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi: robil**a**. Robil erkak, robili esa bir necha kishi yoki hurmatli vy uchun.

u7-l5.6.en.en: Lucia and Emma had breakfast at eight.
u7-l5.6.en.t: Lusiya va Emma soat sakkizda nonushta qilishdi.

en: A few common verbs change more. Learn them as words.
Verbs in **-ieť** change ie to e: vid**ie**ť → vid**e**l. Verbs like stretnúť swap **-núť** for **-ol / -la**: stihnúť → stihol, stihla; zabudnúť → zabudol, zabudla.
t: Koʻp ishlatiladigan baʼzi feʼllar kuchliroq oʻzgaradi. Ularni alohida soʻz sifatida yodlang.
**-ieť** bilan tugaydigan feʼllarda ie → e boʻladi: vid**ie**ť → vid**e**l. stretnúť kabi feʼllarda **-núť** oʻrniga **-ol / -la** keladi: stihnúť → stihol, stihla; zabudnúť → zabudol, zabudla.

u7-l5.8.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the past of byť ends in **-la**: **bola**. Bol is for a man, boli for more people.
u7-l5.8.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun byť feʼlining oʻtgan zamoni **-la** bilan tugaydi: **bola** (edi). Bol erkak, boli esa bir necha kishi uchun.

u7-l5.9.why.en: Tomáš did the meeting, so the verb is for a man: stretnúť → **stretol**. Emmu is just the object; stretla is a woman meeting someone.
u7-l5.9.why.t: Uchratgan — Tomash, shuning uchun feʼl erkak shaklida: stretnúť → **stretol**. Emmu — faqat toʻldiruvchi; stretla esa ayol kimnidir uchratganda aytiladi.

u7-l5.10.prompt.en: What did you do yesterday? (to a man)

en: You're asking a man, so the past tense ends in **-l**: robi**l**. Robila is for a woman.
The question is to ty (you), so the past tense adds **si**: čo **si** robil. Som goes with ja (I).
t: Siz erkakdan soʻrayapsiz, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-l** bilan tugaydi: robi**l**. Robila — ayol uchun.
Savol «sen»ga berilyapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamonga **si** qoʻshiladi: čo **si** robil, «qilding»dagi -ng kabi. Som — ja (men) uchun.

u7-l5.11.question.en: Lucia says this. What did she do?
u7-l5.11.question.t: Lusiya shunday deydi. U nima qilgan?

u7-l5.11.why.en: **Jedla** is the past tense of jesť (ate), and **včera** is yesterday. Eating it now would be jem polievku.
u7-l5.11.why.t: **Jedla** — jesť (yemoq) feʼlining oʻtgan zamoni («yedi»), **včera** esa «kecha». Hozir yeyayotgan boʻlsa, jem polievku derdi.

u7-l5.13.why.en: Formal **vy** always takes **-li** in the past, even for one person like pán Kováč: **boli** ste, never bol ste.
u7-l5.13.why.t: Hurmatli **vy** oʻtgan zamonda doim **-li** oladi, janob Kovach kabi bitta kishiga ham: **boli** ste, hech qachon bol ste emas.

en: To say you didn't do something, add **ne-** to the past form, just like in the present: **ne**robil, **ne**bola, **ne**išli.
som, si, sme, ste still come second: **Nebola som** doma. Včera **som nebola** doma.
t: Biror ishni qilmaganingizni aytish uchun oʻtgan zamon shakliga **ne-** qoʻshing, xuddi hozirgi zamondagidek: **ne**robil, **ne**bola, **ne**išli. U feʼlga qoʻshib yoziladi, oʻzbekchadagi -ma- kabi (qilmadim, bormadi).
som, si, sme, ste avvalgidek ikkinchi oʻrinda turadi: **Nebola som** doma. Včera **som nebola** doma.

u7-l6.1.en.en: Emma wasn't at the lecture yesterday.

u7-l6.1.why.en: Emma is a woman, so the past ends in **-la**, with **ne-** in front for not: **ne**bol**a**. Nebol is for a man, neboli for more people.
u7-l6.1.why.t: Emma — ayol, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi, inkor uchun esa oldiga **ne-** qoʻshiladi: **ne**bol**a**. Nebol erkak, neboli esa bir necha kishi uchun.

u7-l6.2.question.en: Tomáš missed the bus. What does he say?
u7-l6.2.question.t: Tomash avtobusga ulgurmadi. U nima deydi?

u7-l6.2.why.en: Missing the bus is not making it, so add **ne-**: **ne**stihol. Tomáš is a man, so **-ol**; nestihla is for a woman.
u7-l6.2.why.t: Avtobusga ulgurmaslik — inkor, shuning uchun **ne-** qoʻshiladi: **ne**stihol. Tomash — erkak, shuning uchun **-ol**; nestihla esa ayol uchun.

u7-l6.3.prompt.en: I didn't have breakfast today. (man speaking)

en: A man is speaking, so the past tense ends in **-l**: neraňajkova**l**. Neraňajkovala is for a woman.
With ja (I), the past tense adds **som**, in second place: dnes **som** neraňajkoval. Si goes with ty (you).
t: Erkak gapiryapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-l** bilan tugaydi: neraňajkova**l**. Neraňajkovala — ayol uchun.
«Men» uchun oʻtgan zamonga **som** qoʻshiladi, gapda ikkinchi oʻrinda: dnes **som** neraňajkoval. Si — ty (sen) uchun.

en: **už** = already, **ešte** = still. With a “not” they flip: **ešte nie** = not yet, **už nie** = not any more.
t: **už** = allaqachon, endi; **ešte** = hali. Inkor bilan maʼnosi oʻzgaradi: **ešte nie** = hali yoʻq, **už nie** = endi yoʻq.

u7-l6.6.en.en: It's eight o'clock and Lucia is still asleep.
u7-l6.6.en.t: Soat sakkiz, Lusiya esa hali uxlayapti.

u7-l6.6.why.en: **Ešte** means still: Lucia is still asleep. Už spí would mean she's already asleep.
u7-l6.6.why.t: **Ešte** — «hali»: Lusiya hali uxlayapti. Už spí esa «allaqachon uxlab qoldi» degani boʻlardi.

u7-l6.7.why.en: With a not, ešte and už flip: **ešte nie** is not yet, and už nie is not any more. Už on its own means already.
u7-l6.7.why.t: Inkor bilan ešte va už maʼnosi oʻzgaradi: **ešte nie** — «hali yoʻq», už nie — «endi yoʻq». Už oʻzi yolgʻiz «allaqachon» degani.

u7-l6.8.en.en: Have you had lunch? — No, I haven't had lunch yet.
u7-l6.8.en.t: Tushlik qildingmi? — Yoʻq, hali tushlik qilmadim.

u7-l6.8.why.en: Not yet is **ešte** with a not: ešte som **ne**obedovala. Už with a not means not any more.
u7-l6.8.why.t: «Hali» — **ešte**, inkor bilan birga: ešte som **ne**obedovala (hali tushlik qilmadim). Inkor bilan už esa «endi yoʻq» degani.

en: Already is **už**. Ešte means still; with a not, ešte som nejedla is “I haven't eaten yet”.
A woman is speaking, so the past of jesť is **jedla**. Jedol is the form for a man.
t: «Allaqachon» — **už**. Ešte esa «hali»; inkor bilan ešte som nejedla — «hali ovqatlanmadim».
Ayol gapiryapti, shuning uchun jesť feʼlining oʻtgan zamoni — **jedla**. Jedol — erkak uchun shakl.

en: Tomáš is not asleep any more.

u7-l6.11.prompt.en: Were you at the seminar? (to a woman, informal)

en: You're asking a woman, so the past of byť is **bola**. Bol is for a man.
The question is to ty (you), so the past tense adds **si**: bola **si**. Som goes with ja (I).
t: Siz ayoldan soʻrayapsiz, shuning uchun byť feʼlining oʻtgan zamoni — **bola**. Bol — erkak uchun.
Savol «sen»ga berilyapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamonga **si** qoʻshiladi: bola **si**, «boʻlding»dagi -ng kabi. Som — ja (men) uchun.

u7-l6.12.en.en: Lucia, have you been to the library yet? — Not yet.

u7-l6.12.why.en: Not yet is **ešte nie**. Už nie means not any more, as if she used to go and stopped.
u7-l6.12.why.t: «Hali yoʻq» — **ešte nie**. Už nie esa «endi yoʻq» degani, goʻyo u ilgari borib yurgan-u, keyin toʻxtagandek.

u7-l7.1.en.en: The lecture is at half past nine.

en: A woman is speaking, so the past tense ends in **-la**: zaspal**a**. Zaspal is for a man.
With ja (I), the past tense adds **som**: zaspala **som**. Si goes with ty (you).
t: Ayol gapiryapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-la** bilan tugaydi: zaspal**a**. Zaspal — erkak uchun.
«Men» uchun oʻtgan zamonga **som** qoʻshiladi: zaspala **som**. Si — ty (sen) uchun.

u7-l7.3.question.en: Lucia hasn't had breakfast yet. What does she say?
u7-l7.3.question.t: Lusiya hali nonushta qilmagan. U nima deydi?

u7-l7.3.why.en: Not yet is **ešte** with a **ne-** past form: **ne**raňajkovala. Už som raňajkovala means she's already eaten; ešte raňajkujem, she's still eating.
u7-l7.3.why.t: «Hali qilmadim» — **ešte** va **ne-** qoʻshilgan oʻtgan zamon: **ne**raňajkovala. Už som raňajkovala «allaqachon nonushta qildim», ešte raňajkujem esa «hali nonushta qilyapman» degani.

en: The exam is what you have, the object, so skúška changes -a to **-u**: mám **skúšku**.
It's ja (I) who has the exam, so mať ends in **-m**: **mám**. Máš is the ty form (you).
t: Imtihon — sizda bor narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun skúška soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: mám **skúšku**.
Imtihon menda, yaʼni ja, shuning uchun mať **-m** bilan tugaydi: **mám** (menda bor). Máš — ty (sen) shakli.

u7-l7.5.en.en: Emma and Lucia are still asleep.

u7-l7.5.why.en: Emma and Lucia are oni (they), so spať ends in **-ia**: sp**ia**. Spí is for one person, spíme for my.
u7-l7.5.why.t: Emma va Lusiya — oni (ular), shuning uchun spať **-ia** bilan tugaydi: sp**ia**. Spí bitta kishi, spíme esa my uchun.

en: At a time is **o** + the **-ej** form: o siedm**ej**. Sedem is the plain number, for counting.
“We” is my, so stretnúť ends in **-eme**: stretn**eme** sa. Stretnem is the ja form: I'll meet.
t: Soat nechada ekanini aytish uchun **o** + **-ej** shakli keladi: o siedm**ej** (soat yettida). Sedem — oddiy son, sanash uchun.
«Biz» — my, shuning uchun stretnúť **-eme** bilan tugaydi: stretn**eme** sa (uchrashamiz). Stretnem — ja shakli: «uchrataman».

u7-l7.7.en.en: Yesterday Emma and Lucia sat in the library.
u7-l7.7.en.t: Kecha Emma va Lusiya kutubxonada oʻtirishdi.

u7-l7.7.why.en: Emma and Lucia are more than one person, so the past ends in **-li**: sedel**i**. Sedela is for one woman, sedel for one man.
u7-l7.7.why.t: Emma va Lusiya — bir necha kishi, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamon **-li** bilan tugaydi: sedel**i**. Sedela bitta ayol, sedel esa bitta erkak uchun.

u7-l7.8.why.en: Slovak looks ahead: 12:30 is half of the coming hour, one, so **pol jednej**. Pol dvanástej is 11:30, and štvrť na jednu 12:15.
u7-l7.8.why.t: Slovaklar oldinga qarab hisoblaydi: 12:30 — keyingi, birinchi soatning yarmi, shuning uchun **pol jednej**. Pol dvanástej — 11:30, štvrť na jednu — 12:15.

en: First I showered, then I had breakfast.
First I took a shower, then I had breakfast.
t: Avval dush qabul qildim, keyin nonushta qildim.
Avval dushga tushdim, keyin nonushta qildim.

u7-l7.10.en.en: Mr Kováč, have you seen Emma?

u7-l7.10.why.en: Formal **vy** always takes **-li** in the past, even for one person like pán Kováč: **videli** ste. Vidieť also changes ie to e.
u7-l7.10.why.t: Hurmatli **vy** oʻtgan zamonda doim **-li** oladi, janob Kovach kabi bitta kishiga ham: **videli** ste. Vidieť soʻzida ie ham e ga aylanadi.

u7-l7.11.en.en: I wasn't at the seminar yesterday.

u7-l7.12.prompt.en: Did you go to the lecture? (to a man, informal)

en: You're asking a man, so the past of ísť is **išiel**. Išla is for a woman.
The question is to ty (you), so the past tense adds **si**: išiel **si**. Som goes with ja (I).
t: Siz erkakdan soʻrayapsiz, shuning uchun ísť feʼlining oʻtgan zamoni — **išiel**. Išla — ayol uchun.
Savol «sen»ga berilyapti, shuning uchun oʻtgan zamonga **si** qoʻshiladi: išiel **si** (bording). Som — ja (men) uchun.

u7-l7.13.en.en: Tomáš isn't asleep any more, he's already having breakfast.
u7-l7.13.en.t: Tomash endi uxlamayapti, allaqachon nonushta qilyapti.

u7-l7.13.why.en: With a not, **už** means not any more: už nespí, he's no longer asleep. Ešte nespí would mean he isn't asleep yet.
u7-l7.13.why.t: Inkor bilan **už** «endi … emas» degani: už nespí — endi uxlamayapti. Ešte nespí esa «hali uxlagani yoʻq» degani boʻlardi.

u7-l7.15.en.en: Yesterday we were in the library.
